P32: Vascular diseases arise in different anatomical beds but share risk factors and pathological processes, suggesting partly common genetic and cellular mechanisms. Here we integrate public single-cell data into an atlas of 1,175,115 cells and analyse genome-wide association data for eight vascular phenotypes. Genetic covariance separates aortic from atherosclerotic diseases while retaining a shared component. A heterogeneity-filtered multivariate genome-wide association study identifies 155 loci; re-estimation without coronary artery disease identifies 67, with 25 interval components overlapping the primary set. MAGMA and scDRS map the shared signal to selected vascular cell states, with enrichment sensitive to coronary artery disease omission. Cross-disease pseudobulk analysis prioritises 29 gene-cell-state associations, with colocalisation and fine-mapping refining selected candidates. CoVarNet identifies one T-cell composition module meeting structural, coverage and within-study coherence criteria. Target-excluded spatial mapping reveals heterogeneous regional associations, without establishing candidate-specific spatial excess. Together, these analyses provide a common reference for genetic and cellular variation across vascular diseases while separating robust localisation from evidence for causal or candidate-specific effects.
P59: Re-analysis of clusters with conflicting lineage programmes and within-lineage annotation review identified 116 named Level 2 states. The raw Level 2 field contained 118 values; combining these with their parent lineages produced 128 groups, including unresolved or unevaluated groups (Source Data, Figure1/L2_cross_study_recurrence.tsv). Named-state annotation is illustrated in Fig. 1e and Extended Data Figs. 3-5 and documented in Supplementary Tables 3 and 29; study counts for the 16 major lineages are shown in Fig. 1f. These counts do not imply that every group is stable across studies. Genetic enrichment retained 103 eligible Level 2 groups, whereas CoVarNet applied additional recurrence and marker criteria and analysed 89 nodes. State abundance varied across studies and samples (Supplementary Tables 29 and 30), and rare or unresolved labels were assessed separately (Supplementary Table 31). Cell-composition analyses yielded 577 valid models; 52 optimisation failures, 5 models with invalid uncertainty and 182 combinations lacking eligibility were retained in the model audit (Extended Data Fig. 6a,b and Supplementary Tables 35 and 60). Analysis sets differed by question: L1 and L2 communication included 229 and 212 biological specimens; primary pseudobulk analyses used six studies represented by 53 technical records; CoVarNet structure used 223 profiles and disease association 217 profiles; spatial mapping included 35 recorded biological units. These are not interchangeable donor counts (Supplementary Tables 47 and 50). The pan-vascular atlas is available through an interactive resource (https://atlas.panvascularatlas.com/).
P84: Spatial transcriptomics supports regional localisation of candidate signals
P85: We next asked whether candidate gene-cell-state associations from the single-cell atlas could also be observed within intact vascular tissue. We mapped 128 parent-qualified factors to 49 Visium sections from seven public vascular datasets, comprising 35 recorded biological units and 45,348 in-tissue spots across atherosclerotic arteries, aortic valves and other vascular beds (Fig. 5a and Supplementary Tables 21 and 32). GSE248608 and atlas source GSE248609 share a publication and the GSE248610 project, but cross-modality donor identity was unresolved. A current atlas match to GSE306288 was not established, and 16 GSE314851 units were identified at library rather than verified donor level (Supplementary Tables 56 and 57).
P86: The 29 Tier 1 gene-cell-state pairs were evaluated after excluding all candidate identities from reference training and spatial mapping. Of 2,842 prespecified section-posterior-candidate models, 2,044 were estimable. In the primary q05/all-section analysis, 10 abundance terms, 8 regional-programme terms and 1 interaction met FDR<0.05 within the joint 87-test family (Fig. 5b-d and Supplementary Table 32). The abundance associations comprised six positive and four inverse relationships. FN1 showed an inverse fibroblast-abundance association (beta=-0.3439, 95% confidence interval -0.4172 to -0.2705; FDR=1.79 x 10^-18), whereas SCARB1 showed a positive association (+0.1533, +0.0498 to +0.2568; FDR=0.0229). Their primary I2 values were 97.1% and 88.9%, indicating substantial heterogeneity. Nine abundance terms remained significant across posterior-mean and q05 summaries and inclusion or exclusion of two QC-fallback sections (Supplementary Table 53). These are conditional regional slopes, not pseudobulk fold changes.
P87: Spatial interpretation distinguished regional localisation from candidate-specific excess. Target exclusion reduces direct feature circularity but does not resolve source dependence, shared deconvolution or serial-section residual covariance. LIPA, FHL3 and ZNF589 lacked FDR-significant primary abundance associations despite their expression and regulatory support. Across all 14 modules, CM09 showed high raw spatial coherence but did not exceed a strict parent-lineage-matched null (q05 within-spot FDR = 0.545 and six-neighbour FDR = 0.413; Fig. 5e,f and Supplementary Tables 17, 18, 33 and 34). CM03 exceeded this null for six-neighbour coherence (FDR = 0.028), while remaining exploratory under the separate structural-confidence criteria. These results distinguish spatial organisation from coordination beyond parent-lineage composition (Extended Data Fig. 10).
P95: Abundance, communication and spatial analyses supplied tissue context. CM09 met the joint abundance-module criteria and linked T-cell programmes, while the remaining modules stayed exploratory. Its spatial coherence did not exceed the strict parent-lineage-matched null, indicating that high raw coherence alone does not establish autonomous fine-state coordination. Concordant communication support was concentrated in the G2 ascending-aorta comparison and depended on multi-cohort eligibility. Spatial associations differed in direction and sensitivity across the 29 candidates. These findings do not establish causal signalling or candidate-specific spatial enrichment.
P96: Several limitations remain. Public cohorts differed in sampling, tissue processing and sequencing, and disease context was partly linked to anatomical site. Repeated-donor dependence and study-tissue confounding remain relevant, particularly for profile-level CoVarNet coherence. Communication used donor-clustered uncertainty where required; spatial serial sections were pooled without explicit residual covariance modelling. These analyses do not constitute independent replication. Unresolved donor identities were retained as separate recorded units and cannot be regarded as proven independent individuals. The genetic analyses used European-ancestry GWAS summary statistics and require extension to other ancestries. CAD contributed substantial information, and its omission reduced power and the number of shared-factor loci. Available bulk-tissue eQTL resources cannot resolve regulation within individual vascular cell states, and Visium spots represent multicellular regions. Prospective genotype-linked, single-cell and higher-resolution spatial data with detailed pathology will permit more direct causal tests.
